summary: B8: the expedition bridge gains save_json/load_json over ExpeditionState's existing canonical JSON, and CampaignSession gains new_game, save_to_slot, continue_newest and list_slots over user://saves/<slot>.json, with newest decided by the save's own campaign day and strategic hour rather than by file time.

coordination.notes: B16 is changing configure and resolve_midnight in godot_bridge.rs and B17 begin_pending_battle/create_debug_battle; this lane appends two #[func]s at the end of the Project42ExpeditionBridge impl block and touches no existing function there, so all three merge as keep-both tails. Two deliberate departures from the card, both AGENTS.md section 0. (1) The card names the refusal shape `{"ok": false, "reason": ...}` and in the same sentence says to reuse the shape the bridge already uses and not to invent a second one. The bridge has no ok/reason shape: every expedition refusal is `expedition_error_dictionary` -- `{configured: false, error: <code>, metadata: {...}}` -- and that is what load_json answers with, so Godot has one refusal to check on this boundary rather than two. (2) The card asks for the round-trip and refusal logic in a plain Rust function the bridge calls, tested in Rust. That function already exists and is already tested: ExpeditionState::from_json parses, runs validate() and enforces the CURRENT_SAVE_VERSION gate, and expedition.rs already holds boundary_save_reload_preserves_legal_next_commands, ...after_a_route_choice, rejects_a_save_version_from_the_future and rejects_malformed_json. Adding a second helper or a second copy of those tests would be the fork the rule forbids, so load_json calls from_json directly and the bite was run against the existing tests. No new Rust test was written and expedition.rs is byte-identical to trunk. MockSimulationPort was not touched: it extends SimulationPort (the battle bridge, which has no save surface), there is no mock expedition port in the tree, and this lane changed no existing dictionary shape -- load_json returns the snapshot dictionary or the error dictionary that already exist -- so nothing on the mock could drift.
